17 Researchers have developed a new type of filament lamp with an efficiency of 40%. Old-type
filament lamps have an efficiency of 5.0%. The two types of lamp produce the same useful output
power.
What is the ratio input power to new type of lamp
input power to old type of lamp ?
A
0.13
B
0.63
C
1.6
D
8.0

hints: Notice the two lamps produce the same useful output power, but the efficiencies are $40\%$ for the new lamp and $5.0\%$ for the old lamp.
Recall $\text{efficiency} = \text{useful output power} / \text{input power}$, so rearrange to $\text{input power} = \text{useful output power} / \text{efficiency}$ for each lamp.
Write the ratio of the two input powers and cancel the common useful output power, leaving old efficiency divided by new efficiency.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: $\text{eff}_{new} = 40\% = 0.40$, $\text{eff}_{old} = 5.0\% = 0.050$, and let the common useful output power be $P_{out}$.
State the efficiency rule for power: $\text{efficiency} = P_{out}/P_{in}$, so $P_{in} = P_{out}/\text{efficiency}$.
Apply to each lamp: $P_{in,new} = P_{out}/0.40$ and $P_{in,old} = P_{out}/0.050$.
Calculate $0.050/0.40 = 0.125 \approx 0.13$, with no unit as a ratio, and the value is less than $1$ as expected for the more efficient lamp. This is option A.

A.explanation: Ratio equals $5.0/40 = 0.125$, about $0.13$, because the more efficient new lamp needs less input for the same useful output.

B.explanation: Not $0.63$; this does not follow from $\text{input} = \text{useful output}/\text{efficiency}$ with $0.05$ and $0.40$.

C.explanation: Not $1.6$; the new lamp is more efficient so its input power must be smaller, giving a ratio less than $1$.

D.explanation: This is the inverse ratio $40/5.0 = 8.0$, which is input power to old type divided by input power to new type.
